einzeiler: Adam Hamilton and Rob Flaherty discuss election victories and bridging political divides.
kurzfassung: Tim Miller speaks with newly elected Senator Adam Hamilton about his surprising transition from pastoral work to the U.S. Senate and his emphasis on empathy. Later, Rob Flaherty joins the show to analyze the midterm election results, Democratic blowouts in key states, and data center backlash. The conversation explores candidate quality, messaging strategies, and the changing political landscape.
stichpunkte: Adam Hamilton reflects on his unexpected Senate victory in Kansas and his focus on shared human values.
Hamilton discusses his pastoral background and how listening to opposing views can change minds.
Rob Flaherty analyzes the 2026 midterm results, highlighting an anti-status quo sentiment among voters.
The hosts review massive Democratic wins in swing states like North Carolina, Georgia, and Pennsylvania.
Discussion centers on candidate quality, effective communication strategies, and social media presence.
The failure of Republican gerrymandering strategies and the resulting backlash are examined.
Voter pushback against tech money, AI super PACs, and data center expansion is highlighted.

clips.hook: The ease of provoking versus influencing
clips.text: Creating annoyance in public discourse requires no special skill compared to the effort needed to genuinely persuade someone.
A prominent political figure achieves overwhelming support, reshaping local dynamics and freeing up national resources.

beschreibung:
Kansas Senator-elect Hamilton was not recruited out of the Democratic Party pipeline. The Methodist pastor chose to challenge Roger Marshall because he didn't like what was happening in the country, including with ICE agents and cuts to healthcare. But he was also bothered by people in DC claiming to be Christian but not acting like it. Plus: Kamala campaign alum Rob Flaherty joins Tim to celebrate some of the biggest midterm stars, the Dems figuring out how to communicate with voters, the massive blowouts in Georgia, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania—and how Democrats in the new Congress have to address the growing concerns over AI.
Senator-elect Adam Hamilton and Rob Flaherty join Tim Miller.
